stem.en: A thousand families each pay ₹500 a month into a common health fund. In one year, 25 families are treated in hospital and the other 975 never claim. Which statement best explains why the 975 families still gained?

text.en: They will get their own premiums back at the end of the year, because families that do not claim are refunded.
The company invests the premiums during the year and shares the profit with every family that paid.
They bought the right to have a large hospital bill paid, so a loss that would empty one family's savings is shared across many.
They gained nothing, because only the families that actually received money from the fund gained anything.

explanation.en: A premium buys cover, not a refund. The small regular payments of many families make a large loss payable. So a family that falls ill does not have to spend its savings. Every family that paid holds that same right, whether or not it claimed.

hints.en: Think about what each family bought with its ₹500, rather than about what it received back this year.
Which family is protected next year: the one that claimed, the one that did not claim, or both?
